The test image shows a pepper plant with one leaf having a large, water-soaked, brown/tan collapsed lesion on the lower half. The tissue looks papery and wilted, with the rest of the plant remaining green. This rapid tissue collapse pattern points toward Phytophthora Blight or Late Blight as top candidates.

Now I'll view one reference from each of 4 candidate classes.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Pepper plant (green bell peppers visible) with one leaf showing a large, water-soaked, tan-brown collapsed lesion occupying the lower half. Rest of plant is healthy green. Bugwood image #5605081.
- **Phytophthora_Blight ref (Bugwood_21)**: Same pepper crop, same sandy field setting — shows stem collapse from Phytophthora capsici. Adjacent reference (5604954) is nearly sequential to the test image (5605081), strongly suggesting same collection.
- **Phytophthora_Blight ref (Bugwood_100)**: Field-level view of dying pepper plants — confirms this class targets pepper crops.
- **Late_Blight ref**: Shows similar water-soaked brown leaf collapse, but on tomato/potato, not pepper.
- **Bacterial_Wilt ref**: Bacterial streaming test — completely different symptom type.

The large water-soaked collapsed leaf lesion on a pepper plant, from the same Bugwood pepper disease collection, is characteristic of **Phytophthora capsici** foliar blight. The sequential Bugwood IDs strongly link this to the Phytophthora_Blight class.
